name: Pearl's Bagels & Bakery
founded_note: I LOVE NY says it opened in Albany in December 2021; same storefront since then not confirmed
note: Small-batch scratch bakery making hand-rolled, boiled and baked vegan bagels plus challah pockets; walk-in only, Wednesday to Sunday mornings.

name: Broad Street Bagel Co.
founded_note: Its site says the family opened it in Kinderhook in 2012 using a 150-year-old Brooklyn bagel recipe
note: Family-owned Kinderhook village bagel shop making kettle-boiled, Brooklyn-style bagels in a renovated old building; a second shop is in Slingerlands.

name: Rhinebeck Bagels
founded_note: Its site says it has been family owned and operated in the village since 1995; same storefront throughout not confirmed
note: Family-run village bagel shop for breakfast and lunch, eat-in or takeout.

name: Broadway Gourmet Bagel Cafe & Caterers
founded_note: I LOVE NY's listing says it was established in 1992 in Massapequa; same storefront throughout not confirmed
note: North Massapequa bagel cafe and caterer that rolls its bagels by hand, with flagels, bialys and novelty sweet bagels.

name: Nyack Hot Bagels
note: Rockland bagel shop and deli on Route 59 known for hand-rolled, boiled and baked bagels served hot from the oven.

name: West End Bagels
note: Clifton Park bagel shop whose owners trained with downstate bagel makers; bagels made from scratch every morning, plus bialys.

name: The Gourmet Bagel Co.
founded_note: Opened September 2025, per Newsday; the owners' first Gourmet Bagel shop opened in Brooklyn Heights in 1994 and they also run one in Bohemia
note: Riverhead bagel shop that boils and bakes its bagels the old-fashioned way (no rack oven), using the recipe from the owners' Brooklyn shop.

name: Fantzye Bagels
founded_note: Opened its Kingston shop in November 2024 after starting as a Martha's Vineyard pop-up in 2020
note: Midtown Kingston shop that ferments sourdough bagels for three days, shapes them by hand, boils them and bakes them on cedar boards.

name: Moonrise Bagels
founded_note: The business began in Woodstock in 2021 (idea on New Year's Eve 2020); its site calls Tinker Street the original location
note: Woodstock bakery that hand-rolls, boils and bakes New York-style bagels stuffed with fillings like pizza; now also in Poughkeepsie and Manhattan.

name: Ben's Kosher Delicatessen
founded_note: Ben's says it has served kosher deli since 1972; this location's opening year isn't stated
note: Family-run kosher deli and restaurant group that cures its own corned beef; one of its Long Island dining rooms.

name: Ben's Kosher Delicatessen
founded_note: Ben's says it has served kosher deli since 1972; this location's opening year isn't stated
note: Family-run kosher deli and restaurant group that cures its own corned beef; one of its Long Island dining rooms.

name: Lido Kosher Deli
founded_note: Its site says it has served Long Island for nearly 60 years; run by the Goetz family
note: Full-service kosher deli in Long Beach with a takeout counter, catering and nationwide shipping; Newsday singles out its pastrami.

name: Regal Kosher Deli
founded_note: Opening year not stated on its site
note: Kosher deli, restaurant and caterer on Old Country Road in Plainview.

name: Ben's Kosher Delicatessen
founded_note: Ben's says it has served kosher deli since 1972; this location's opening year isn't stated
note: Family-run kosher deli and restaurant group that cures its own corned beef; one of its Long Island dining rooms.

name: Pastrami N Friends
founded_note: Newsday (Apr 2025) and its site say Ernie Quartarone opened it in Commack in 1975; same address since then not confirmed
note: Kosher deli in Commack named for its signature sandwich, run by Ernie Quartarone and partner Ronnie Roman.

name: Epstein's Kosher Deli
founded_note: Its site says the family has cooked the original Epstein's recipes since 1969; year at this address not stated
note: Small family-run kosher deli, restaurant and caterer on Central Avenue under rabbinic supervision.

name: King Umberto
founded_note: Its site and Newsday (June 2025) say it opened in 1976 (Ciro Cesarano and Rosario Fuschetto) at Meacham Ave and Hempstead Tpke, expanding in 1987; a Jan 2026 Newsday piece says 1975
note: Elmont pizzeria-restaurant credited by Newsday as the first place to sell grandma pizza; slices of regular, Sicilian and grandma at the counter, and a tasting-menu room (Serata) in the old dining room.

name: Taglio
dishes: Roman pizza al taglio by the piece
founded_note: Newsday (June 2025) calls it Rob Cervoni's six-year-old spot
note: Mineola pizzeria that is half classic New York slice shop, half Roman pizza-al-taglio counter.

name: Mama's of Copiague
founded_note: Newsday (Aug 2026) says it marks 50 years in 2026; a second location opened in Carle Place
note: Italian-American restaurant and pizzeria selling slices from grandma to specialty pies alongside big pasta plates.

name: Umberto's
founded_note: Opened November 2025 in the former Bellagio Pizzeria space, per Newsday; Umberto's itself was founded in New Hyde Park in 1965 by brothers Umberto and Carlo Corteo
note: Suffolk outpost of the Long Island Umberto's pizzeria family, a contender for 'home of grandma pizza', with a counter pizzeria selling slices and a sit-down room.

name: Canepa's Pizza Shop
note: Warrensburg pizzeria making daily-mixed dough from Italian family recipes, with classic New York thin-crust slices.

name: Hot Dog Charlie's
founded_note: Its site says the family business began in 1922 as New Way Lunch; this location's opening year isn't stated
note: Family-run mini hot dog shop known for its chili meat sauce; this is the Cohoes shop.

name: Gus's Hot Dogs
founded_note: Its site says it has served mini hot dogs and hamburgers with its meat sauce for over 60 years
note: Walk-up window in Watervliet serving 4-inch Capital District mini dogs plain or with the works, plus burgers.

name: Mama's Boy Burgers
note: Catskills burger spot that also serves Hoffman's hot dogs, both all-beef and white hots.

name: Hot Dog Charlie's
founded_note: Its site says the family business began in 1922 as New Way Lunch; this location's opening year isn't stated
note: Family-run mini hot dog shop known for its chili meat sauce; this is the Rensselaer shop.

name: Famous Lunch
dishes: mini hot dogs with meat sauce, mustard and onions
founded_note: Its site says it opened as Quick Lunch at 111 Congress Street in 1932 and was renamed Famous Lunch after a 1958 episode
note: Downtown Troy lunch counter serving the Capital District's mini hot dogs since 1932.

name: Hot Dog Charlie's
founded_note: Its site says the family business began in 1922 as New Way Lunch; this location's opening year isn't stated
note: Family-run mini hot dog shop known for its chili meat sauce; this is the Lansingburgh shop.

name: First Prize Mike's
founded_note: Its site says it has served Schenectady for over 75 years
note: Family-run Schenectady diner-style restaurant built on its hot dog with meat sauce; I LOVE NY lists it among Capital District mini-dog spots.

name: New Way Lunch
dishes: hot dog with mustard, onions and meat sauce
founded_note: Founded August 1919 in Glens Falls by John Floro, per its site, which calls South Street its first location; year at this exact address not stated
note: Family-run Glens Falls hot dog counter serving dogs on steamed rolls with mustard, onions and its own meat sauce; a second shop is in Warrensburg.

name: Walter's Hot Dogs
dishes: split, griddled hot dog with Walter's mustard sauce
founded_note: Serving hot dogs since 1919; its site says the copper-roofed pagoda stand on Palmer Avenue was built in 1928
note: Walk-up hot dog stand in a copper-roofed Chinese pagoda on the National Register, splitting and griddling beef-pork-veal dogs; open year-round.

name: Stissing House
founded_note: Its site says the building went up in 1782 as a tavern with rooms and a domed ballroom; it declined after World War I and reopened as a restaurant in 1995
note: Pine Plains tavern building from 1782, restored in the 1990s and run since 2022 by chef-proprietor Clare de Boer, with an upstairs ballroom for events and cooking classes.

name: The Tavern at the Beekman Arms
founded_note: Wikipedia says the tavern (begun 1704 by William Traphagen) moved to this crossroads in 1766; the inn claims to be America's oldest continuously operated inn, and the Village marked its 260th anniversary in July 2026
note: Colonial-era tavern inside the Beekman Arms inn at Rhinebeck's main crossroads, serving lunch, brunch and dinner every day of the year.

name: Hudson House River Inn
founded_note: Its site says the building dates to 1827 and has welcomed guests since 1832, and calls it the second-oldest continuously operated inn in New York State (a claim)
note: Riverfront inn at the foot of Cold Spring's Main Street with two dining rooms (the River Room and the Half Moon Tavern) serving lunch, dinner and Sunday brunch.

name: Bear Mountain Inn
founded_note: Built and opened in 1915 inside Bear Mountain State Park (on the National Register); it was closed for renovation about 2006-2012, per Wikipedia
note: Rustic-style 1915 park inn run by the Palisades Interstate Park Commission, with a full-service restaurant and bar and seasonal festivals.

name: The Old '76 House
founded_note: Its site says the building dates to 1668 and calls it America's oldest restaurant/tavern (a claim); it figures in the 1780 Major Andre story
note: Colonial-era tavern in Tappan, restored by the Norden family, serving lunch and dinner with live music most nights.

name: Claudio's
season: Spring to fall (2026: waterfront opened April 24, restaurant May 1)
founded_note: Claims 'Est. 1870' at the foot of Main Street on Greenport Harbor; new management runs it today
note: Harborfront seafood restaurant, bar and marina at the foot of Greenport's Main Street, dating its start to 1870.

name: Mohonk Mountain House
founded_note: Its site says the Smiley family founded it in 1869; a National Historic Landmark resort
note: Historic lakeside mountain resort above New Paltz with a main dining room; day-visit passes include dining options.

name: Royal Dim Sum
founded_note: Opened early 2025 in the Samanea Mall, per Newsday (Mar 2025)
note: Full-service Cantonese dim sum hall in Westbury's Samanea Mall with chefs from Hong Kong and Guangzhou, live seafood tanks and weekend carts.
